ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Anna uses 32 small grey squares to frame a $7 \mathrm{~cm}$ by $7 \mathrm{~cm}$ big picture. How many small grey squares does she have to use to frame a $10 \mathrm{~cm}$ by $10 \mathrm{~cm}$ big picture?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The picture shows a square drawing surrounded on all four sides by a grey frame. The grey frame is exactly one small square thick around the square picture. Reasoning: The text says a 7 cm by 7 cm picture uses 32 grey squares. With a one-square-thick frame, the outer square would be 9 by 9, so the number of grey squares is 9^2 - 7^2 = 81 - 49 = 32, matching the given information. For a 10 cm by 10 cm picture with the same one-square-thick frame, the outer square is 12 by 12. The number of grey squares is 12^2 - 10^2 = 144 - 100 = 44.
